scenes.title: 1997 Fribourg / Science Landmark: The 3-Row Dopamine Raster Plot — +Burst at Surprise, 0 Flat at Expected Juice, −Dip When Withheld!
scenes.era: 1997, Institute of Physiology, University of Fribourg, Switzerland

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1997 neurophysiology gallery featuring an **articulated matte-white porcelain macaque sculpture** seated calmly before a **Conditioned Cue Lamp & Sweet Fruit-Juice Dropper**, paired with the monumental **3-Row Schultz-Dayan-Montague Raster Plot Display**: **Row 1 (No Cue + Juice = +Burst!)** | **Row 2 (Cue -> Expected Juice = Burst at Cue, 0 FLAT at Juice!)** | **Row 3 (Cue -> No Juice = Sharp −DIP Below Baseline!)** alongside the equation **`δ = Actual − Expected`**.

positions.who: Wolfram Schultz (mannequin in 1997 crisp white laboratory coat over shirt and tie)
positions.where: standing beside the illuminated 3-Row Dopamine Raster Display pointing to Row 2's completely flat trace at the moment expected juice arrives

positions.who: Peter Dayan & Read Montague mannequins (in 1997 computational academic blazers holding Temporal-Difference RL notebooks)
positions.where: matching the live VTA neuron spikes directly onto Sutton & Barto's reinforcement-learning equation beside the articulated matte-white porcelain macaque model!
positions.facing: beside conditioning apparatus and equation board

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain macaque sculpture at Cue Lamp + Juice Dropper panel
props.period_detail: stages the classic Fribourg behavioral conditioning setup cleanly per R46 porcelain-animal rule

props.name: 3-Row Dopamine Raster Plot Board ('+Surprise | 0 Expected | −Withheld' + 'δ = Actual − Expected')
props.period_detail: the single most famous figure in modern computational neuroscience

actions.verb_sequence: Row 1: surprise juice drop triggers a sharp VTA +Burst -> Row 2: Cue Lamp flashes (+Burst at lamp!) followed 1.5s later by expected juice (**VTA stays dead flat at 0!**) -> Row 3: Cue Lamp flashes, juice is withheld, and VTA firing **plunges below baseline** right on the 1.5s mark!

reactions.reaction: light up seeing biological neurons run exact Temporal-Difference AI math
confirms: 'Dopamine isn't pleasure — it is pure surprise math!'

scenes.wardrobe: 1997 European & computational academic attire: crisp white lab coat and dark tie; tweed blazers and button-down shirts.
scenes.recognition_hook: Give unexpected apple juice and dopamine explodes — ring a reliable bell first so the juice is 100% expected, and when that delicious juice hits the tongue, dopamine stays dead flat at zero!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1997 neurophysiology gallery with an articulated matte-white porcelain macaque sculpture at a cue-lamp juice panel beside Wolfram Schultz pointing to a 3-row '+Surprise / 0 Expected / -Withheld' dopamine raster plot

scenes.title: Why Smartphone Feeds & Slot Machines Never Go Flat: Variable Rewards!

layout.description: Sunlit studio contrasting a Predictable Scheduled Paycheck (`1 − 1 = 0` flat dopamine) against an Unpredictable Pull-to-Refresh Feed (`Actual ≠ Expected` -> endless `+δ` and `-δ` swings!).

positions.where: seeing why unpredictable notifications hijack VTA `Wanting` even when zero real `Liking` remains

props.name: Predictable (0 Error) vs Variable-Ratio Slot Machine (+/− Swings) Card
props.period_detail: explains 1 AM doomscrolling via Schultz's equation

actions.verb_sequence: pulls-to-refresh repeatedly chasing an unpredictable +δ hit -> switches red notification badges OFF

reactions.reaction: instant relief once the artificial prediction-error loop breaks

scenes.recognition_hook: Why can you scroll at 1 AM without enjoying a single post? Because unpredictable feeds hijack dopamine 'surprise-wanting' while pleasure sits at zero!

actions.verb_sequence: align biological cue-transfer curves with AI value-function learning
